Hi Ella — thanks for the note and the RFP.

High level options (short table below) — happy to put numbers into your spreadsheet (attached) once you confirm which path you'd prefer:

Option A — Seat-based HSM + Tiered Audit Retention (recommended for predictable ops)
- HSM: per-seat annual license (covers node provisioning and attestation); seats convert to a monthly amortized charge on invoice.
- Audit logs: tiered retention buckets (30d included, 90d low $/GB, 365d mid $/GB, 7yr archival by request).
- Commits: 12-month commit with quarterly true-ups; usage floor = 70% of committed throughput to avoid month-to-month volatility.
- Discount: baseline 10% on add-ons for 12-month commit; higher discounts for larger commits (we can run scenarios).

Option B — Usage-floor + variable HSM pass-through (lower upfront, higher variable)
- HSM: pass-through pricing by HSM provider with Redwood margin; no per-seat amortization.
- Audit logs: pay-as-you-go with monthly true-up; retention expansion billed at month-end.
- Commits: no seat commit, recommend a 3-month pilot then review.

Quick clarifying asks so we can finalize numbers:
1) Expected concurrent HSM sessions / keys (estimate)
2) Audit log ingestion rate (GB/day) and desired retention horizon per environment (prod/stage)
3) Preferred commit length (3/12/24 mo)

Ella / team — adding a few specifics from the packaging side so you can share with legal/procurement:

- Audit log retention: Standard package includes 30 days at no additional charge. Tier 2 (31-365 days) priced at $0.015/GB/month in the example workbook; Tier 3 (366-2555 days) available by request and typically treated as archival storage with lower $/GB but retrieval fees.
- HSM: Our recommended approach (Option A) is per-seat licensing so we can guarantee SLAs and key-holder separation. We amortize the seat over the contract term and map to an equivalent monthly line item so it behaves like a subscription for your finance team.
- Residency surcharge: US-only region default is no surcharge; cross-region or sovereign entitlements (EU/APAC) trigger additional residency fees.
- True-up cadence: We generally do quarterly true-ups for 12-month commits and monthly true-ups for month-to-month plans.

Hi Ella — Ben here (security economics). Two brief operational notes that typically influence which pricing path we recommend:

1) HSM seat cap: If MediVance expects a predictable key-holder model (<10 seats) we strongly recommend per-seat licensing (Option A). This keeps attestation and patching responsibilities within Redwood and simplifies SOC evidence. For spiky workloads (lots of ephemeral keys) a usage-based pass-through may be cheaper but adds billing variability.

2) Evidence & audit delivery: For long retention windows (365+ days) customers often prefer a fixed monthly retention fee vs raw $/GB to make forecasting easier. We can offer a blended Tier 2 fixed-rate option (example: $X/month for up to Y GB/day ingestion, then $0.01/GB overage) as a middle ground.

Commercial ask: If MediVance can commit to 12 months and agree to a 70% usage floor on throughput, we can offer: 12% discount on compliance add-ons and a $30k onboarding credit applied to the first two invoices (to offset seat amortization).

Happy to hop on a short call to walk procurement/legal through the workbook.
